note: Rodent diabetes models predicted durable glucose lowering; patients on MK-0941 and AZD1656 lost the effect within months, and only later hepatoselective or dual-acting drugs held it.
label: T2D (GCK activators)

engagement.note: The first GK activators lowered glucose in rodent diabetes models; this opens the rodent track later compared for MK-0941 (the 2003 compound is a non-member sibling).
engagement.short: GKAs lower glucose in diabetic rodents
engagement.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Sibling compound (RO-28-1675), not a member.
engagement.judgement: Class model opened at the first GKA rodent paper; the compound is a non-member sibling.

engagement.note: MK-0941 cut post-challenge glucose up to 48% in dogs and mice; added to insulin glargine in patients, 2-h postmeal glucose fell 37 mg/dL.
engagement.quote: Maximal placebo-adjusted least squares mean changes from baseline in A1C (baseline A1C 9.0%) and 2-h PMG were -0.8% and -37 mg/dL (-2 mmol/L), respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both papers. Fasting glucose did not move in patients.
engagement.judgement: No direct GK occupancy readout exists; the models' own readout was glucose, so the tier is downstream. Paired Eiki 2011 (same drug) with Meininger 2011.
engagement.magnitude_basis: post-challenge glucose: dog OGTT AUC -48% vs patient 2-h PMG -37 mg/dL

engagement.note: PK/PD model built from sinogliatin healthy-volunteer data and a second GKA's patient data to project glucose profiles for the first-in-patient study.
engagement.quote: In this study, we propose a methodology to predict pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic profiles of sinogliatin (HMS-5552, RO-5305552), a novel glucokinase activator to treat diabetes mellitus, for first-in-patient (FIP) studies.
engagement.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: the first-in-patient study it was built for (NCT02077452) started March 2014.
engagement.judgement: Opener dated to the first-in-patient study the projection was made for, not to the 2016 publication.
engagement.model: Translational PK/PD model for sinogliatin (dorzagliatin), scaled from healthy-volunteer data and another GKA's patient data

engagement.note: Projected PK/PD parameters in patients fell within 70-130% of observed for five of seven, the rest within twofold. Retrodiction rule: first public in 2016, after GK activation had lowered glucose in patients (MK-0941, 2011).
engagement.quote: Results showed that the projected pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic values of five parameters were within 70-130% of values fitted from observed clinical data while the other two remaining projected parameters were within a twofold error.
engagement.magnitude_basis: projected vs fitted PK/PD parameters in T2D patients
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (Clin Pharmacokinet, paywalled). That the projection was fixed before the 2014 first-in-patient data were seen is the paper's learn-research-confirm framing, not verified; NCT02077452 has no posted results.
engagement.judgement: Engagement is a target-level claim: the model was first public after another GKA's patient glucose result, so retro, as the checker adjudicated.
engagement.model: Translational PK/PD model for sinogliatin (dorzagliatin), scaled from healthy-volunteer data and another GKA's patient data

dose.note: Rodent models set glucose-lowering doses; no human exposure, regimen or margin was stated (MK-0941 later stayed effective 16 days in mice, Eiki 2011).
dose.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no stated human exposure target found.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the rodent model's dose basis.

dose.note: A model fitted to LY2599506's patient multiple-dose data picked titrated Phase 2 doses; observed HbA1c and hypoglycaemia matched. Dose retrodiction rule: LY2599506's own Phase 2 results were posted (2011-10-26) before the model was published (2012).
dose.quote: The predictions were in reasonable agreement with the observed clinical data.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; both Phase 2 trials (NCT01024244, NCT01029795) were terminated early for nonclinical safety findings.
dose.judgement: Own model_id track. The same drug's own Phase 2 result was public before the model, so retro, not same.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted vs observed 3-month HbA1c and hypoglycaemia

dose.note: The same model projected HbA1c response at the first-in-patient regimens.
dose.quote: In this study, we propose a methodology to predict pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic profiles of sinogliatin (HMS-5552, RO-5305552), a novel glucokinase activator to treat diabetes mellitus, for first-in-patient (FIP) studies.
dose.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy (first-in-patient study start, March 2014).
dose.model: Translational PK/PD model for sinogliatin (dorzagliatin), scaled from healthy-volunteer data and another GKA's patient data

dose.note: Projected one-month HbA1c fall at the dosed regimens matched patients (0.82 vs 0.78%). Dose retrodiction counts only the drug's own earlier patient result; dorzagliatin's patient data were first public in this paper, so it stays same.
dose.quote: The predicted HbA1c changes were nearly identical to observed clinical values (0.82 vs. 0.78%).
dose.magnitude_basis: projected vs observed 1-month HbA1c change (0.82 vs 0.78%)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only. Whether this model, rather than the Phase 1b data alone, set the Phase 2 doses (NCT02561338) is not verified.
dose.judgement: Checker proposed retro; under the dose ruling only dorzagliatin's own earlier public patient result could make it one, and none was public before Dec 2016 (only the 2016 healthy-volunteer SAD, the model's input), so same.
dose.model: Translational PK/PD model for sinogliatin (dorzagliatin), scaled from healthy-volunteer data and another GKA's patient data

efficacy.note: GK activators lowered glucose in several rodent diabetes models; opens the rodent track later compared for MK-0941.
efficacy.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.

efficacy.note: Combination design: MK-0941 added to insulin glargine met its 14-week HbA1c primary endpoint (-0.8%), scored on that primary; the response was gone by week 30.
efficacy.quote: At Week 14, A1C and 2-h postmeal glucose (PMG) improved significantly versus placebo with all MK-0941 doses.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change at the primary time point
efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint governs, so the week-14 win is same; the 30-week loss is recorded as partial, not scored.

efficacy.note: AZD1656 monotherapy missed its 4-month HbA1c primary endpoint after early glucose falls faded; rodent models had shown sustained lowering. The later add-on-to-metformin trial (NCT01020123) is listed under patient_trials.
efficacy.quote: The changes from baseline to 4 months in HbA1c were not significant for the AZD1656 40-200 mg group versus placebo [mean (95% CI) placebo-corrected change: -0.22 (-0.65, 0.20)%; p = 0.30].
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. AstraZeneca later ran its own rodent models for up to 11 months and found durable lowering 'in marked contrast to clinical findings' (Baker 2014, doi 10.1111/bph.12504).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sustained glucose lowering in rodents vs non-significant 4-month HbA1c in patients

patient_trials.quote: Addition of AZD1656 (individually titrated) to metformin gave significant improvements in glycaemic control up to 4 months, although efficacy diminished over time.

efficacy.judgement: One drug's contra beats MK-0941's same on the same rodent model. Baker 2014 is a retrodiction that also failed (contra) and confirms the call; not entered separately to avoid a repeat status.

efficacy.model: People with GCK-activating or GKRP loss-of-function variants
efficacy.note: Combination design: TTP399 (cadisegliatin) on stable metformin cut HbA1c 0.9% over 6 months, scored on the primary. Rule 6: topline public in a vTv press release on 10 Aug 2016, before Vella 2019.
efficacy.quote: In this 6-month study, TTP399 (800 mg/day) was associated with a clinically significant and sustained reduction in glycated hemoglobin, with a placebo-subtracted least squares mean HbA1c change from baseline of -0.9% (P < 0.01).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; sponsor-authored. Year from the vTv press release (10 Aug 2016): 'Topline results showed achievement of the primary endpoint of statistically significant change from baseline in HbA1c at 6 months'. model_first_use_year 2016 is a proxy; the genetic rationale guided TTP399's design earlier but no earlier public date was verified. AGATA (NCT02405260) has no posted results.
efficacy.judgement: The human-genetic rationale is its own model_id, limited to the drug designed from it (TTP399); dorzagliatin's Phase 3s moved to the islet track's dorzagliatin entry, since dorzagliatin is not hepatoselective.

efficacy.note: Human islets perifused with dorzagliatin and MK-0941, after both drugs' trials had reported.
efficacy.quote: A comprehensive approach using human islet perifusions, enzyme kinetics, X-ray crystallography, and modeling studies was applied to compare the effects of dorzagliatin with those of the unsuccessful GKA MK-0941 (Merck Pharmaceuticals), which is well characterized both clinically and mechanistically.
efficacy.confidence_note: First use dated to this paper.
efficacy.model: Human islet perifusion with enzyme kinetics and structural modelling (dorzagliatin vs MK-0941)

efficacy.note: Dose- and glucose-dependent insulin secretion with dorzagliatin in human islets matches its Phase 3 HbA1c success, which the authors set out to explain.
efficacy.quote: Dorzagliatin dose-dependently reduces the glucose threshold for stimulation of insulin secretion and binds preferably to the closed form of GK, preventing overstimulation of the enzyme.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: islet insulin secretion vs Phase 3 HbA1c response
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only. The paper explains success vs failure mechanistically; it does not reproduce MK-0941's loss of effect over time, so only the dorzagliatin half is scored. Patient side: Zhu 2022 SEED, online 2022-05-12. Patient side: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-022-01802-6.
efficacy.judgement: Islet model run after dorzagliatin's Phase 3 primaries were public, so retro; comparison_stated true because the paper frames itself as explaining the clinical success.
efficacy.model: Human islet perifusion with enzyme kinetics and structural modelling (dorzagliatin vs MK-0941)

patient_trials.quote: At week 24, the least-squares mean change in glycated hemoglobin from baseline (95% confidence interval) was -1.07% (-1.19%, -0.95%) in the dorzagliatin group and -0.50% (-0.68%, -0.32%) in the placebo group
In patients with T2D who experienced inadequate glycemic control with metformin alone, dorzagliatin resulted in effective glycemic control with good tolerability and safety profile

efficacy.note: Opens the rodent track for AZD1656: the class rodent models were the basis on which AZD1656 entered patients.
efficacy.short: Rodent models in use for AZD1656
efficacy.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
efficacy.confidence_note: Proxy opener: no AZD1656 rodent paper public before its trials was found; year held at the track's first comparison (2012) because entries are appended, not reordered.
efficacy.judgement: Split of the rodent efficacy track by drug: AZD1656 gets its own opener.

efficacy.model: Human islet perifusion with enzyme kinetics and structural modelling (dorzagliatin vs MK-0941)
efficacy.note: Human islets perifused with MK-0941 alongside dorzagliatin, after MK-0941's trials had reported.
efficacy.quote: A comprehensive approach using human islet perifusions, enzyme kinetics, X-ray crystallography, and modeling studies was applied to compare the effects of dorzagliatin with those of the unsuccessful GKA MK-0941 (Merck Pharmaceuticals), which is well characterized both clinically and mechanistically.
efficacy.confidence_note: First use dated to this paper.
efficacy.judgement: Split of the islet efficacy entry by drug: opener for the MK-0941 track.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: islet insulin secretion vs week-14 HbA1c change
efficacy.model: Human islet perifusion with enzyme kinetics and structural modelling (dorzagliatin vs MK-0941)
efficacy.note: MK-0941 drove insulin secretion even at low glucose in human islets, consistent with its met 14-week HbA1c primary on insulin glargine (Meininger 2011); the islets do not reproduce the loss of effect by week 30.
efficacy.quote: Dorzagliatin improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in a dose- and glucose-dependent manner, in contrast to MK-0941, which induced maximal insulin secretion at low doses and glucose concentrations.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only. The paper calls MK-0941 'unsuccessful'; the pairing with its met primary endpoint is ours. Patient side: https://doi.org/10.2337/dc11-1200.
efficacy.judgement: Run 14 years after MK-0941's primary was public, so retro; partial because durability, which failed in patients, is not modelled.

safety.note: Rodent diabetes models carried the class into patients; early papers report efficacy, not lipid or liver harm.
safety.quote: In several rodent models of type 2 diabetes mellitus, GKAs lowered blood glucose levels, improved the results of glucose tolerance tests, and increased hepatic glucose uptake.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no nonclinical toxicology review available (no member has an FDA NDA).

safety.note: After MK-0941 (added to insulin glargine) raised triglycerides in patients, nine GKAs raised hepatic and plasma lipids and caused fatty liver in db/db mice and rats. Rule 6: De Ceuninck was online in 2012.
safety.quote: MK-0941 was associated with an increased incidence of hypoglycemia and elevations in triglycerides and blood pressure.
safety.judgement: De Ceuninck (online 2012) postdates MK-0941's own triglyceride signal (2011), so retro on the MK-0941 track. Hypoglycaemia and blood pressure not scored: no model statement found.

safety.note: The rodent lipid warning (2012) held for dorzagliatin: hyperlipidaemia 14% vs 9% in DAWN (online May 2022), significant in a 2024 meta-analysis; fatty liver not measured in patients. Rule 6 dates it to DAWN.
safety.quote: Notably, dorzagliatin had significant effects on the occurrence of hyperlipidemia (OR 1.476, 95% CI 1.025-2.126) and hyperuricemia (OR 2.727, 95% CI 1.523-4.883) in the subgroup analyses.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Liang 2024 (tier 4). Earliest public comparison: DAWN, Yang 2022 (doi 10.1038/s41591-022-01803-5, online 2022-05-12): 'The incidence of hyperlipidemia AEs was 14% in the dorzagliatin and metformin group and 9% in the placebo and metformin group.' AstraZeneca's rodent models (Baker 2014) showed no triglyceride rise.
safety.reason: Lipid harm predicted, seen in patients
safety.judgement: Own track for dorzagliatin: MK-0941's track (retro, then Baker 2014 contra) does not carry over. The rodent prediction predates dorzagliatin's own data, so prospective; partial agreement (lipids yes, steatosis unmeasured).
safety.magnitude_basis: hyperlipidaemia odds ratio vs rodent plasma/hepatic triglycerides

safety.note: Human islets perifused with dorzagliatin and MK-0941, after both drugs' trials had reported.
safety.quote: A comprehensive approach using human islet perifusions, enzyme kinetics, X-ray crystallography, and modeling studies was applied to compare the effects of dorzagliatin with those of the unsuccessful GKA MK-0941 (Merck Pharmaceuticals), which is well characterized both clinically and mechanistically.
safety.confidence_note: First use dated to this paper; earlier human-islet GKA work exists but was not searched for a member-drug comparison.
safety.judgement: Opener; the system was run on member drugs only after their trials.
safety.model: Human islet perifusion with enzyme kinetics and structural modelling (dorzagliatin vs MK-0941)

safety.note: MK-0941 drove maximal insulin secretion at low glucose in human islets, reproducing the excess hypoglycaemia seen in patients (Meininger 2011).
safety.quote: Dorzagliatin improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in a dose- and glucose-dependent manner, in contrast to MK-0941, which induced maximal insulin secretion at low doses and glucose concentrations.
safety.magnitude_basis: insulin secretion at low glucose in islets vs hypoglycaemia incidence in patients
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only. The abstract calls MK-0941 'unsuccessful' but does not itself name hypoglycaemia; the pairing with Meininger 2011 (MK-0941 increased hypoglycaemia) is ours, hence comparison_stated false. Patient side: https://doi.org/10.2337/dc11-1200.
safety.judgement: Run 14 years after MK-0941's hypoglycaemia was public, so retro, not same.
safety.model: Human islet perifusion with enzyme kinetics and structural modelling (dorzagliatin vs MK-0941)

safety.note: GWAS variants in GCK and GCKR used as proxies for GK activation to test lipid, MASLD and CAD effects.
safety.quote: We selected independent genetic variants of GCKR and GCK associated with fasting plasma glucose (FPG) as instrumental variables, to mimic the effects of impaired GK-GKRP interaction and direct GK activation, respectively.
safety.judgement: Opener; run after GKA trials had shown raised triglycerides.
safety.model: Drug-target Mendelian randomization with GCK (direct activation) and GCKR (GK-GKRP disruption) variants

safety.note: Genetic proxy for direct GK activation predicted no dyslipidaemia; GKA trials pooled showed raised triglycerides (meta-analysis 2023) and dorzagliatin raised hyperlipidaemia risk.
safety.short: GCK proxy misses GKA lipid rise
safety.quote: Genetically-proxied GK activation was associated with decreased risk of CAD (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.88) and not with dyslipidemia.
safety.magnitude_basis: predicted lipid effect of GK activation (none) vs triglyceride rise in GKA trials
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only. The authors attribute the trial hypertriglyceridaemia to GK-GKRP disruption (their GCKR proxy, which did predict it) rather than to GK activation; which member drugs disrupt GKRP is not established, so the call depends on reading the GCK proxy as the class proxy. Patient side: https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2023.1175198.
safety.judgement: Scored on the GCK proxy, the paper's stand-in for the class mechanism: it predicted no dyslipidaemia, patients on GKAs showed it, and a retrodiction that fails is contra. The GCKR arm would score retro under the authors' reading.
safety.model: Drug-target Mendelian randomization with GCK (direct activation) and GCKR (GK-GKRP disruption) variants

safety.magnitude_basis: plasma triglycerides: no rise in rodents vs rise in MK-0941 patients
safety.note: Two AstraZeneca GKAs given chronically to Zucker rats and gk(wt/del) mice raised neither plasma nor hepatic triglycerides, failing to reproduce MK-0941's triglyceride rise in patients (2011).
safety.quote: This efficacy was achieved without increases in plasma or hepatic triglycerides, accumulation of hepatic glycogen or impairment of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Baker 2014 (PMID 24772484, BJP April 2014), quoted; compounds unnamed in the abstract. Patient side Meininger 2011: 'MK-0941 was associated with an increased incidence of hypoglycemia and elevations in triglycerides and blood pressure.'
safety.judgement: Checker adjudication on safety 3, settled per track: Baker 2014 post-dates MK-0941's own triglyceride result and failed to reproduce it, so contra on the MK-0941 track; it does not carry to dorzagliatin's track.

safety.note: Opens the rodent track for dorzagliatin: HMS5552 was dosed for a month in T2D rats with cholesterol and triglycerides measured (2017).
safety.quote: The levels of total cholesterol, triglyceride, fasting plasma insulin (FINS), and glucagon (FG) were determined, and an oral glucose tolerance test was performed.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only; its lipid result is not stated in the abstract. The rat study was public in Jan 2017; the year is held at the track's first comparison (2022) because entries are appended, not reordered.
safety.judgement: Split of the rodent safety track by drug: dorzagliatin gets its own opener.
